text.p: The Estonian parliament on Wednesday approved a 12.5 billion kroon 1997 budget, which by law has to be balanced.
The budget package received the backing of 62 members of the 101-seat parliament and 32 deputies voted against it.

The biggest revenue items are sales tax worth 5.79 billion kroons, personal income tax of 2.25 billion kroons and company tax worth 1.1 billion kroons. The government also forecasts excise duty revenue of 983 million kroons.
The education ministry takes up most spending at 2.2 billion kroons, the welfare ministry 2.184 billion and the interior ministry has spending of 1.546 billion kroons.

Estonia is considered one of the most convinced reformers of the former Soviet Union, with a successful privatisation programme under its belt and a strong commitment to fiscal and budgetary prudence.
Economic growth next year is expected to be around three percent and inflation should fall to around 14 percent, from a year-on-year 16.4 percent in November.
